newsitem.title: CHINA: China blasts Japan over proposed war shrine.
newsitem.headline: China blasts Japan over proposed war shrine.

text.p: China lashed out on Monday at a plan by a Japanese group to build a shrine to soldiers killed in World War Two, saying it could lead to resurgent militarism in Japan.
The new shrine could raise the risk of Tokyo repeating its ruinous wartime aggression, the official Guangming Daily said.
"This kind of thinking will unavoidably mislead a whole generation of Japanese and increase the danger that Japan will follow the same old road to ruin," the newspaper said.
The plan by a right-wing Japanese group to build the hall to fallen warriors would not reflect the suffering Japan's imperial army inflicted on its Asian neighbours, it said.
China also slammed a proposal by groups under Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) to invite foreign heads of state and dignitaries to visit shrines to Japanese war dead.
Such suggestions had hurt the feelings of people in China and other Asian countries, state radio quoted Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai as saying.
"We once again express our outrage and condemnation at the actions of relevant groups of the Liberal Democratic Party," the radio quoted Cui as saying.
"We hope Japan can truly reflect on that period's history of militarism and foreign aggression," Cui said.
The new shrine would only focus on the difficulties Japanese soldiers and their families faced in the war while neglecting the suffering of Asian countries invaded by Japan, the newspaper said.
"It does not reflect Japan's invasion of Asian countries and peoples or its history of devastation," it said.
China indignantly protested against a visit by several Japanese cabinet ministers to a shrine dedicated to Japan's war dead last August on the 51st anniversary of Japan's World War Two surrender.
Beijing has expressed concern over what it sees as resurgent militarism in Japan and accuses Tokyo of trying to whitewash its wartime atrocities.
China estimates up to 35 million Chinese were killed or wounded by invading Japanese troops from 1931 to 1945.
